name: unity-mcp
description: Hot-reloadable multi-agent Unity MCP server with a bounded bootstrap and searchable canonical typed-tool catalog.
long_description:
AnkleBreaker Unity MCP connects Claude, Codex, and other MCP hosts to your Unity Editor through a canonical, instance-bound tool catalog. This repository is independently maintained while retaining the attribution required by the AnkleBreaker Open License.

**Key features:**
- Stable stdio launcher hot-reloads server implementation changes without restarting the MCP host
- Bounded bootstrap with instance binding, Unity Hub, health, and list/search/get discovery
- Intent-ranked discovery followed by exact typed-tool activation with full schemas
- Unity, package, and project tools share one catalog contract and one connection binding
- Multi-instance support: run multiple Unity Editors simultaneously, auto-port selection (7890-7899), shared instance registry
- ParrelSync clone detection for multiplayer development workflows
- Multi-agent async queue with fair round-robin scheduling
- Read batching (up to 5/frame) and write serialization (1/frame)
- Agent session tracking and action logging
- Project Context discovery for project-aware AI assistance

**Requires the companion Unity Editor plugin:** Install via Unity Package Manager -> Add package from git URL -> `https://github.com/VM233/VMUnityMCP.git`

After installing the package, configure local bridge and port settings under Preferences -> Unity MCP, then use `unity_list_instances` to confirm the Editor is reachable.

unity_hub_path.title: Unity Hub Path
unity_hub_path.description: Path to Unity Hub executable. On Windows: C:\Program Files\Unity Hub\Unity Hub.exe - On macOS: /Applications/Unity Hub.app/Contents/MacOS/Unity Hub

bridge_port.title: Bridge Port
bridge_port.description: Default port for the Unity Editor plugin. With multi-instance support (v2.15.0+), ports are auto-discovered from the instance registry. Only used as fallback. Default: 7890

tools.name: unity_list_instances
tools.description: List registered Unity Editor instances, including reload status and current reachability. Returns each instance's project name, port, Unity version, and whether it's a ParrelSync clone. Use this to see which Unity projects are currently open before selecting one to work with.

tools.name: unity_select_instance
tools.description: Select which Unity Editor instance to work with for this session. All subsequent unity_* commands will be routed to the selected instance. Provide a port returned by unity_list_instances. A later call may still override the target with its own port or expectedProjectPath.

tools.name: unity_hub_list_editors
tools.description: List all Unity Editor versions currently installed via Unity Hub, including their installation paths.

tools.name: unity_hub_available_releases
tools.description: List Unity Editor versions available for download from Unity Hub.

tools.name: unity_hub_install_editor
tools.description: Install a specific Unity Editor version. Optionally include platform modules (android, ios, webgl, linux, macos, windows-il2cpp).

tools.name: unity_hub_install_modules
tools.description: Install additional platform modules to an already-installed Unity Editor version.

tools.name: unity_hub_get_install_path
tools.description: Get the current default installation path for Unity Editors.

tools.name: unity_hub_set_install_path
tools.description: Set the default installation directory for Unity Editors.

tools.name: unity_mcp_health
tools.description: Inspect the Unity MCP host binding and canonical catalog state without changing Unity. Use this before discovery when connection or project ownership is uncertain.

tools.name: unity_tools_list
tools.description: Browse the canonical Unity MCP tool catalog by module or category. Call without filters for bounded module and category counts; this tool never returns full schemas.

tools.name: unity_tools_search
tools.description: Find canonical typed Unity MCP tools from a natural-language task. Returns a small ranked set with boundaries, required arguments, preconditions, and side effects but no full schemas.

tools.name: unity_tools_get
tools.description: Get the complete contract for one canonical Unity MCP tool and activate that typed tool for direct invocation. Use an exact name returned by unity_tools_search or unity_tools_list.

prompts.name: setup_scene
prompts.description: Set up a basic Unity scene with common elements
prompts.text: Help me set up a Unity scene. Start by checking the connection to Unity, then show me the current hierarchy. Ask what kind of scene I want to create (e.g., 3D platformer, FPS, puzzle game) and set up appropriate GameObjects, lighting, and a camera.

prompts.name: profile_and_optimize
prompts.description: Profile the project and suggest optimizations
prompts.text: Profile my Unity project and help me optimize it. Start the profiler, take a memory snapshot, check the console for warnings, and analyze the results. Give me specific, actionable recommendations for improving performance.
